title: William Stephenson telegram about Townsend Brown's mission into Germany
summary: Jesse Michels tells of William Stephenson telegram about Townsend Brown's mission into Germany, about 1945 at Nazi Germany, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: and there's a telegram from um him to Josephine, who's Townsend Brown's wife,
when Thomas Townsend Brown did a tech retrieval mission in behind enemy lines in World War there's a telegram from William Stevenson to Townsend's wife Josephine and he says your husband is okay.
tellings.difference: Quotes the telegram as saying 'your husband is okay' and calls the mission a tech retrieval; it does not credit Jan Lundquist.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the telegram from William Stephenson to Josephine Brown about Townsend Brown's mission behind enemy lines.

as_told.title: Townsend Brown parachuting into Nazi Germany and the Stephenson telegram

plain: Podcast host Jesse Michels says that near the end of World War Two, an American scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown went behind enemy lines into Nazi Germany to retrieve technology. Michels says there is a telegram from William Stephenson, a wartime intelligence figure, to Brown's wife Josephine, telling her that her husband is okay. In one telling he credits a researcher named Jan Lundquist for this. In another he just quotes the telegram and calls the trip a tech retrieval mission, and he offers it as proof that Brown took part in secret wartime work.
